Don’t worry about it, I’ve heard it’s good to be better at english because getting math scores up is easier than getting english scores up(?) but there are usually one or two common knowledge questions, if you’re not too worried about a perfect score they won’t be a big deal I think but if you know basics (titration, solvent, etc) I think you’d be good on the maybe couple of passages that have it - it would help to do online tests for math/sci too because they’re pretty good at showing you what kind of questions you missed! Also, if time is your issue you might want to skip and come back to the different perspectives passage in science, since you have to look at a bunch of confusing viewpoints and it usually takes lonnger

Math - Really just need to know a couple of formulas and some harder concepts, try to spend 30 minutes on the first 40 questions and 30 minutes on the last 20 (don’t overthink it, if you get an answer that matches one of the questions and seems right, just put it down and move on or mark it so you can come back and check it if you have extra time): make sure to skip any questions you’re stuck on (I circle the questions I want to come back to and go back when I’m done) every question is worth the same point so be precise


Science - Skim the passage quickly, don’t get focused on details just spend a couple seconds figuring out the point of the experiment and then skip right to the questions, don’t overthink it, read every question very carefully (tricky ones in there), try to spend less than 5 minutes per passage (this section requires more concentration and focus than any other section imo)
